subject: Mutual Action Plan & staging sprint sequencing — StrataCommerce
messages:
From: Anya Kovalenko <anya@stratacommerce.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@stratacommerce.com>
Date: 2026-09-14T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Onboarding next steps — request for MAP and milestone dates

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked the latency profile and the proposal. Were preparing our internal onboarding calendar and need a concise Mutual Action Plan that lines up deliverables, owners, and target dates for a staging pilot. Can you share a MAP that: 
- Breaks work into sprints (preflight, staging, pilot, go-live)
- Identifies Redwood owners vs our (Strata) owners
- Flags dependencies (network, security, data access)
- Suggests integration windows that minimize customer downtime

If possible, send a spreadsheet we can drop into our program tracker. Procurement will review timing as part of the SOW.

Appreciate it —
Anya

Anya Kovalenko
Head of Product Operations | StrataCommerce
anya@stratacommerce.com
+1 (415) 555-0133

From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: Anya Kovalenko <anya@stratacommerce.com>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@stratacommerce.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-14T13:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Onboarding next steps — request for MAP and milestone dates

Hi Anya / Tom —

Attached is a first-cut Mutual Action Plan (Strata_MAP_v1.xlsx). Quick highlights in-line below and next-step suggestions: 

• High-level plan: 4 sprints over 6 weeks (Preflight 1 week / Staging 2 weeks / Pilot 2 weeks / Go-live prep 1 week).
• Owners: Redwood (Olga = PM, Marcus = Integration Lead, Monica = CS Lead). Strata owners marked in the sheet — please confirm who will own Data Access and Network approvals.
• Dependencies:
  - Network: VPC peering + firewall rules (we recommend a maintenance window during staging week 2).
  - Data: scoped dataset for pilot (anonymized).
  - Security: SOC-2 evidence and limited audit access for the pilot.
• Integration windows: recommended nightly 10pm–2am PT for cutover tasks to keep retail traffic unaffected. See integration_windows.csv for proposed dates.

Next steps I propose:
1) You review the MAP and mark rows that require Strata sign-off (owners/date).
2) Procurement reviews the SOW draft (I attached SOW_Draft_20260916.docx).
3) Marcus and your engineering lead sync to confirm the nightly windows — can we book a 30-min call tomorrow?

Ill leave action items in the top sheet of the workbook.

Thanks —
Olga Petrov
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
olga@redwood.com
Attachment: Strata_MAP_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 120KB)
Attachment: SOW_Draft_20260916.docx (docx, 95KB)

From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: Anya Kovalenko <anya@stratacommerce.com>, olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-15T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan & staging sprint sequencing — StrataCommerce

Anya / team —

Thanks for the MAP — I reviewed the integration notes and have two technical clarifications before we lock windows: 
1) Do you have a preferred IP allowlist flow for peering (static IPs vs. NAT gateway)? If NAT, we need rough throughput numbers for sizing.
2) For the pilot dataset: can you confirm the expected max sequence length and request concurrency (even ballpark)? That determines whether we recommend the 1:1 staging node ratio or a 2x buffer.

Im free for a 30-min sync tomorrow 10:30–11:30 PT if that works. Ill also populate the "integration" tab in the MAP with explicit tasks and estimated hours.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Integration Lead, Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com

From: Anya Kovalenko <anya@stratacommerce.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com, olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@stratacommerce.com>, Procurement <procurement@stratacommerce.com>
Date: 2026-09-15T13:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan & staging sprint sequencing — StrataCommerce

Marcus —

Thanks. Quick answers: 
• IP model: we prefer NAT gateway behind static egress IPs (we can provide 2 static egress IPs). Expected sustained throughput ~200 Mbps during seeding; spike concurrency up to ~30 concurrent requests during testing.
• Pilot dataset: up to 4096 token sequences; training data will be pre-sliced and anonymized.

Tomorrow 10:30 PT works; joining: myself, Tom, and our infra lead (I will share contact in the calendar invite). Procurement will review the SOW after your sync.

— Anya

From: procurement@stratacommerce.com
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: Anya Kovalenko <anya@stratacommerce.com>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@stratacommerce.com>, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-20T16:04:00Z
Subject: Re: SOW draft and MAP — a couple quick commercial clarifications

Hi Olga —

Procurement had two quick clarifications on the SOW before legal takes the redline: 
1) Can you confirm whether the pilot falls under the same pricing band as hosted consumption or if theres a pilot credit applied? We need a short note in the SOW.
2) SLA exceptions: procurement is requesting a 30-day trial-style SLA carveout for pilot (reduced uptime guarantee) — can Redwood confirm and we will include the agreed language.

We also received the MAP spreadsheet and see the owner columns; please ensure the topo/owner cell for "Network approvals" has Redwood and Strata contacts listed.

If those items are addressed we can route to legal for redlines.

Thanks,
Procurement Team | StrataCommerce
procurement@stratacommerce.com
